taskDescription: At therapeutic doses, about 90 percent of paracetamol is safely glucuronidated or sulphated and excreted; the small remainder is oxidised by CYP2E1 to the reactive electrophile NAPQI, which glutathione conjugates immediately for excretion as a mercapturic acid. Arrange the causal sequence of events that follows an overdose, when this normal handling is overwhelmed.
paragraphs: Conjugation capacity (sulphation, then glucuronidation) is exceeded, and more paracetamol is shunted through CYP2E1, increasing NAPQI production.
Glutathione is consumed faster than it is made and becomes depleted.
Free NAPQI binds covalently to hepatocyte proteins, especially mitochondrial proteins.
Mitochondria fail, oxidative stress rises and ATP is lost.
Centrilobular (zone 3) necrosis follows, where CYP2E1 is most concentrated and oxygen tension is lowest.

overallFeedback.feedback: This sequence shows why paracetamol is safe at normal doses but lethal in overdose: once conjugation pathways saturate and glutathione is depleted, NAPQI attacks mitochondrial proteins, mitochondria fail, and zone-3 necrosis follows, reflecting high CYP2E1 concentration and low oxygen in the centrilobular region. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) supplies cysteine for glutathione synthesis and protects best when started within 8 hours; it can still benefit patients after liver injury has begun.
